advisor.summary: The 2019 tri-agency final rule created the Individual Coverage HRA: an employer of any size reimburses individual-market premiums and out-of-pocket medical care, tax-free to employees, deductible to the business, and subject to no statutory dollar cap. ACA integration is built in — every participant must be enrolled in individual-market coverage or Medicare. Allowances may differ across the regulation's defined employee classes but must be uniform within each class, and no class may be offered a choice between the ICHRA and a traditional group plan. As with every §105/§106 arrangement, >2% S corporation shareholders, partners, and sole proprietors cannot participate tax-free — C-corp owner-employees can. The engine models the employer's deduction for reimbursements; employee-side exclusion value and premium-tax-credit displacement are weighed off-model.
mechanics: The employer sets a fixed monthly allowance per class; employees substantiate individual-market enrollment and their expenses; reimbursements are excluded under §106(a) and §105(b) and deducted under §162(a).

Classes must be drawn from the permitted list in Reg. §54.9802-4 — full-time, part-time, salaried, hourly, seasonal, geographic rating area, among others — with same-terms treatment inside each class, variable only by age (up to 3:1) and family size.
An affordable ICHRA offer extinguishes the employee's §36B premium tax credit; the offer must carry an annual opt-out so an employee facing an unaffordable allowance can preserve the credit.
For applicable large employers, an affordable ICHRA satisfies the §4980H employer-mandate offer; an unaffordable one invites §4980H(b) assessments as employees decline and claim credits.
Minimum class sizes apply to certain classes when a traditional group plan is offered to another class — the regulation's guardrail against pushing risk onto the exchanges.

Owner mapping: C-corp owner-employees participate tax-free; §1372 keeps >2% S corporation shareholders (and self-employed owners generally) out — their route is §162(l), and only the entity's deduction for reimbursements enters the model.

authority.note: The ICHRA regulation: permitted classes, the same-terms rule, the individual-coverage enrollment requirement, and the opt-out right (2019 tri-agency final rule).
Exclude both the reimbursements and the coverage itself from employee income.
The employer's deduction for reimbursements — the only quantity the engine models.
Premium-tax-credit coordination: an affordable ICHRA offer bars the credit; an unaffordable one permits opt-out and a PTC claim.
The employer mandate an affordable ICHRA offer can satisfy for applicable large employers.
Bars >2% S corporation shareholders from tax-free participation by treating them as partners.
IRS guidance on the ICHRA's interaction with the employer mandate and §105(h).

requirements: Every participant (and each covered dependent) enrolled in individual-market coverage or Medicare, substantiated at enrollment and again with every reimbursement.
A written plan with classes drawn solely from the regulation's permitted list and same-terms allowances within each class.
No class offered both the ICHRA and a traditional group plan.
The 90-day advance annual notice explaining premium-tax-credit interaction and the opt-out right.
Minimum class sizes honored where a group plan remains for another class.
risks: Substantiation is the leading failure: reimbursing employees who dropped their individual coverage makes the payments taxable and threatens group-health-plan status with §4980D exposure at $100 per affected individual per day — Reg. §54.9802-4 and Notice 2018-88 draw the compliance boundary.
Improvised classes or minimum-class-size violations forfeit the design's protection.
For applicable large employers, an unaffordable allowance ripens into §4980H(b) assessments as employees decline and take the premium tax credit.
For heavily subsidized workforces, an affordable ICHRA can be worth less to employees than the credits they surrender — model the workforce before replacing group coverage.
Set owner expectations early: pass-through owners get no tax-free self-reimbursement, and the modeled number is the entity deduction alone.
stateNotes: Conformity: states conforming to federal income definitions exclude the reimbursements from employee income just as federal law does, and the employer deduction follows the ordinary business-income computation.
PTET: for pass-through sponsors, the reimbursement deduction reduces the entity income a PTET election is computed on — sequence the two rather than stacking them.
Missouri: conforms through RSMo §143.121; a Missouri pass-through that elects the SALT Parity Act PTET (RSMo §143.436) computes that tax after taking this deduction.
reviewChecklist: Workforce survey supports the ICHRA over group coverage or a QSEHRA, premium-tax-credit displacement math included.
Class design verified line-by-line against Reg. §54.9802-4, minimum class sizes checked.
90-day notice delivered and documented; substantiation workflow running with the administrator.
Affordability computation on file where the client is an applicable large employer.
Owner participation limited to those the exclusion actually reaches.

client.teaser: Set a fixed health budget and let each employee pick the coverage that fits their life.
client.headline: Health benefits on a budget you control — no group plan needed
plainEnglish: Group health insurance means one plan for everyone and a premium hike every year. There is another way. Your business gives each employee a set monthly allowance, tax-free, to buy the health plan they choose on the individual market.
Every dollar is deductible to the business. You set the budget, so renewals bring no surprises. And employees keep coverage that belongs to them, not to the job.

You can set different allowance amounts for different groups — full-time and part-time, for example — as long as everyone in a group is treated the same. A business of any size can use it, and there is no cap on the allowance.
client.analogy: Instead of buying one bus everyone must ride, you hand out travel money and let each person pick the ride that gets them home.
benefits: Deductible to the business, tax-free to employees
You set the budget — no more renewal shock
Works at any company size, with no dollar cap
Employees keep coverage they picked themselves
steps: WE test the ICHRA against your current coverage and your team's facts.
WE design the classes, allowances, plan documents, and required notices.
YOU collect proof of coverage through the administrator and pay reimbursements monthly.
WE revisit the allowances each year as premiums move.
clientCommitments: Reimburse only employees who show current proof of their own coverage
Deliver the annual employee notice on schedule
Tell us before changing who gets which benefit level

annualMaintenance: Annual allowance reset against individual-market premium movement
Affordability re-test wherever the employer mandate applies
